question.text: The Atlanta Compromise was criticized as weak by W.E.B. Du Bois and other co-founders of this American civil rights organization. Thurgood Marshall represented this group in arguments before the Supreme Court, including Brown v. Board.
question.answerHtml: NAACP (accept National Association for the Advancement of Colored People)
question.clue: Ralph David Abernathy was first part of this group before he led the SCLC.

swap.text: This man served as president of Princeton from 1902 to 1910 before being elected U.S. president in 1912.
swap.clue: Louis Brandeis helped to create his New Freedom platform and he won his second term on the slogan, "He kept us out of war".

question.text: Woodrow Wilson created this set of proposals, including freedom of the seas and self-determination, for the postwar world. They were mostly ignored in actual treaties.
question.clue: This speech advocated the elimination of secret treaties, colonial adjustment, and reduction in arms.

swap.text: Washington was invited by this President, who took office after the death of William McKinley. In his military career, this man fought with the "Buffalo Soldiers" as leader of the Rough Riders.
swap.clue: This president summarized his foreign policy, "Speak softly and carry a big stick."

question.leadin: This structure's completion was delayed for many years due to the "Cucaracha Slide" at the Culebra Cut, one end of which was the Chagres River.
question.text: Name this structure, whose construction included the damming of the Chagres River to form Lake Gatun.
question.clue: The Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty provided a strip of land twenty miles wide for this structure, whose construction was supervised by George Washington Goethals.

swap.leadin: Name the following world leaders present at the Paris peace conference.
swap.text: This man represented the United States and was president during World War I. He had won election as a dark-horse candidate in 1912, and he was succeeded by Warren G. Harding.
swap.clue: Late in this man's presidency, the Justice Department arrested and deported radicals in the Palmer raids.

question.leadin: The nomination of one candidate in this election was affirmed in the "smoke-filled room" and supported by his campaign organizer Harry Daugherty.
question.text: Name this election in which Warren Harding's promises of a "Return to Normalcy" earned him a landslide victory.
question.clue: At the Blackstone Hotel in Chicago, a nomination during this election was decided in a "smoke-filled room" by Harry Daugherty.

swap.leadin: Deborah Blum's The Poison Squad focuses on the work of Dr. Harvey Washington Wiley, who is often known as the "father" of this law.
swap.text: Name this act which regulated sanitary standards and prohibited the mislabeling of certain consumables. It was passed alongside the Meat Inspection Act.
swap.clue: The Supreme Court held that it did not apply to therapeutic claims in United States v. Johnson.

question.text: This newly appointed Secretary of State under Theodor Roosevelt was at the meeting with college football leaders. This Nobel Prize winner helped secure Japanese agreement for the Open Door Policy in China.
question.clue: He had already worked as McKinley's secretary of war, but his best-known work came in another cabinet post.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the La Follette family.
swap.text: "Fighting Bob" ran for president in 1924 under a short-lived political party of this name. A former president running for a party with this name finished second behind Woodrow Wilson in the 1912 presidential election.
swap.clue: Perhaps the greatest electoral successes of a party by this name came earlier, in California, where Hiram Johnson was elected governor and then Senator on its banner.

question.leadin: This president declared that "the chief business of the American people is business."
question.text: Name this president who promoted laissez-faire economics despite supporting government intervention as governor of Massachusetts. This "silent" president vetoed the McNary-Haugen Farm Relief Bill while in office.

swap.leadin: After suffering a stroke, this person read a premature obituary claiming they died "broke, alone, and unpopular,"which some people claim led to a second, fatal stroke.
swap.text: Name this Jamaican activist who created the Black Star Line to encourage African Americans to return to Africa as part of the Back-to-Africa movement.
swap.clue: James Wormley Jones' investigation into this man led to his arrest for mail fraud in connection with his Black Star Line shipping company.

question.leadin: History has not looked fondly at some of the people Warren G. Harding appointed to his cabinet.
question.text: Harding may have mistakenly chosen this cabinet member, whose illegal leasing of federal lands was investigated by Thomas Walsh during the Teapot Dome Scandal.
question.clue: As a result, those two became the first two senators from his state, New Mexico, where he owned the massive Tularosa ranch at Three Rivers.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the presidency of Woodrow Wilson.
swap.text: This "Fighting Quaker" was Wilson's attorney general from 1919 to 1921, in which post he contributed to the "red scare" by leading namesake "raids" to gather up political dissidents.
swap.clue: Acting Secretary of Labor Louis Post undid many of this man's actions, which included a crackdown on the Union of Russian Workers for producing an anarchist manifesto.

question.leadin: A split arose between this movement and preservationism, which did not advocate the use of national lands for industry as well as for setting them aside for their natural beauty.
question.text: Name this movement, one of whose members was George Perkins Marsh, a precursor of environmentalism that saw success with the establishment of Yellowstone National Park.
question.clue: A program named for this cause was headed by Robert Fechner and employed young men in tent camps.

swap.text: In 1925, this man moved south to sell deeds to the reclaimed Everglades, but the deeds he sold were actually for worthless upstate swampland. One of this man's earlier plans involved the resale of international postal coupons.
swap.clue: Clarence Barron's expose in the Boston Post calculated that this man must have purchased 160 million items, out of a worldwide supply of only 27,000, for his claimed strategy to work.

question.leadin: The editor of this newspaper managed to convince Mayor James M. Curley to shut down productions of The Clansman, but was unable to halt the premiere of Birth of a Nation at the Tremont Theatre a decade later.
question.text: Name this militant Black newspaper that operated out of the former home of The Liberator. An editor of this newspaper was arrested after verbally sparring with Booker T. Washington during a chaotic 1903 speech.
question.answerHtml: The Boston Guardian [accept The Guardian] (Washington’s 1903 speech to the Boston branch of the National Negro Business League devolved into the chaotic, but peaceful, “Boston Riot.”)

swap.text: According to Adamic, one of the key players in California's "healing industry" was this evangelist, who converted an abandoned church in Echo Park into the Angelus Temple.
swap.clue: Earlier, she had travelled the country with her mother in a special car which had the messages "Where Will You Spend Eternity" and "Jesus Is Coming Soon" painted on it.

question.text: The earlier planned suburb of Coral Gables, Florida was developed entirely under the principles of this turn-of-the-century American urban planning philosophy that arose contemporaneously with the Garden City movement and inspired the McMillan Plan for redesigning Washington D.C.

swap.leadin: She was the first president of the Negro Fellowship League, which provided assistance to black migrants in the north, and her life's work was chronicled in A Red Record and Crusade for Justice.
